target_customer: Security teams at fast-moving and enterprise companies, including Fortune 500 firms
problem: Legacy DLP tools flood lean security teams with false positives while employees keep sharing sensitive data and emailing source code to personal inboxes.
product_category: AI-native data loss prevention and insider risk management

founders.name: Ansh Gupta
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; bio gives no education or employers.

founders.name: Aditya Iyengar
founders.background_notes: YC page lists software engineering roles at those companies.

competitors.name: Cyberhaven
competitors.what: Data lineage based DLP and insider risk
competitors.funding_then: 88M Series C June 2024 at 488M valuation per its press release

technical_complexity.rationale: Endpoint and SaaS data movement telemetry, behavior context and agentic triage with low false positives, plus SOC 2 and enterprise deployment, is hard for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations with identity and security stacks and compliance certification create stickiness, but funded rivals already had data lineage and insider risk products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded rivals keep raising (Above Security 50M in 2026 and Jazz 61M per search results). No acquisition of Candor was found.

market_need_then: Insider risk, shadow AI and alert fatigue with legacy DLP were prominent concerns, and the company claims Fortune 500 testimonials on its site.

branding.domain_note: Uses candor.security, a security TLD, instead of candor.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, punchy, direct; FAQ titled Candid Answers (site copy).

branding.brand_signature: Candid Answers FAQ plays on the name

rebrands.why: not stated; reported by a third-party profile only

brand_strength.rationale: Name is confusable with several other Candor companies, but the plain-speaking voice fits the name. No press on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Candor Security is active with 3 to 5 people and shows enterprise testimonials and SOC 2 Type II on its site, but no priced funding round was found and no exit or layoffs were reported. It competes with well funded rivals such as Cyberhaven and newer AI DLP entrants, so its path depends on landing enterprise logos.
notes: Dealroom lists a 125K seed with no investor and one profile names Y Combinator and Transpose Platform as backers; neither confirmed by a company or press source, so no round is recorded. Third-party profile lists Adarsh Ambati as CEO and co-founder, but he is not named on the YC page or company site I opened, so he is not listed as a founder here. YC page says founded 2024. Haleum former name is from a third-party profile only. Different company from Candor (usecandor) and CandorIQ.
